content.user_title: Write Clear, Efficient AI Agent Prompts
content.value_statement: Many prompts waste the model attention budget with verbose, unstructured instructions that lower output quality. This skill applies Anthropic context engineering principles to help you write clear, high-signal prompts and context files.
actual_capabilities: Explains context engineering principles for curating high-signal tokens during model inference.
Provides Markdown structure standards for organizing prompts into clear semantic sections.
Offers writing style rules that favor direct, imperative language over verbose prose.
Describes just-in-time context loading and progressive information discovery.
Includes reusable context file templates for agents, commands, and general prompts.
Lists common prompt anti-patterns to help authors review and improve their work.
limitations: Provides written guidance and templates only; it does not run code or automate any task.
Focuses on prompt structure and clarity, not on domain-specific model tuning.
The principles are general and may need adaptation for specialized use cases.
It does not measure or benchmark prompt performance for you.

use_cases.title: Author a new agent context file
use_cases.description: A developer uses the templates to create a well-structured context file for a new AI agent with clear roles, tools, and constraints.

use_cases.title: Review and tighten an existing prompt
use_cases.description: A prompt author checks a bloated system prompt against the anti-pattern list and trims redundant instructions to improve clarity.

use_cases.title: Teach prompt engineering standards
use_cases.description: A team lead shares these standards to align a team on consistent, high-quality prompt writing practices.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a core principle
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the context engineering principle of signal-to-noise ratio and give one example of a high-signal and a low-signal instruction.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a context section
prompt_templates.prompt: Using these standards, draft the Instructions section for an agent that validates and stores user contact forms.

prompt_templates.title: Review an existing prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the following system prompt against these standards and list every anti-pattern you find with a suggested fix: [paste prompt here]

prompt_templates.title: Design a just-in-time loading strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Redesign this agent prompt to use just-in-time context loading instead of embedding the full product catalog. Show the before and after and explain the token savings.

output_examples.input: Explain the signal-to-noise principle with an example.
output_examples.output: Signal-to-noise ratio means keeping only tokens that drive the desired outcome. High signal: Validate user input before processing. Low signal: You should always make sure to validate the user input because invalid input could cause problems later on.

output_examples.input: Review this instruction: You might want to consider using the calculate_tax tool if needed.
output_examples.output: This instruction is vague. It uses hedging words like might and consider. A direct rewrite is: Use the calculate_tax tool with amount and jurisdiction parameters.

best_practices: Organize prompts into clear semantic sections using Markdown headers.
Use direct, imperative language and remove hedging words like might or could.
Load detailed information only when needed instead of dumping all data up front.
anti_patterns: Writing long, verbose explanations where a short bulleted list would be clearer.
Loading large data blocks into the prompt before they are actually needed.
Using vague instructions with words like might, could, or should consider.

faq.question: What is context engineering?
faq.answer: Context engineering is the practice of curating the smallest set of high-signal tokens that maximize the chance of the desired model outcome.

faq.question: Who is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for developers, prompt engineers, and team leads who write or review prompts and context files for AI agents.

faq.question: Does this skill run any code?
faq.answer: No. It provides written standards, templates, and guidance only. It does not execute code or automate tasks.

faq.question: Which AI tools does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Claude Code, and Codex, since the standards apply to any prompt or context file.

faq.question: What are the key principles it teaches?
faq.answer: It teaches that context is a finite resource, that prompts should optimize for signal over noise, and that information should be loaded just in time.

faq.question: How do I use the templates?
faq.answer: Copy the relevant template for an agent, command, or general prompt, then fill in each section with clear, direct, and minimal content.
